Call search_docs('operation') and get_doc_file on the Routine/operation model files
to understand ALL operation types (fetch, click, input_text, js_evaluate, download, etc.).
You CANNOT dispatch experiments until you understand the full routine capabilities.

After reviewing docs:
1. Analyze the exploration summaries
2. Call plan_routines to declare what routines to build
3. Use dispatch_experiments_batch to test ALL priority-1 routines IN PARALLEL
4. Record findings for each, then batch the next round
5. Build and submit_routine for each proven routine
6. Call mark_complete when all routines are shipped or failed

IMPORTANT: Always use dispatch_experiments_batch (not dispatch_experiment) to run multiple experiments in parallel. This is much faster.

arguments.usage_guide:
This catalog provides high-level scraping access to key public Premier League APIs observed on premierleague.com. Use them as building blocks:

1) pl_standings — league tables
   - When: You need the current standings table for a competition/season (e.g., to render the Premier League table or power analytics).
   - Input: competitionId (e.g., 8 for PL), seasonId (e.g., 2025).
   - Output: JSON with matchweek and tables[].entries including team, overall/home/away stats and points.
   - Typical flow: Call pl_standings first to know team positions and IDs, then join with team or match data from other routines.

2) pl_fixtures_by_matchweek — fixtures/schedule
   - When: You need all fixtures in a given matchweek for a competition/season (for schedules, previews, or content planning).
   - Input: competitionId, seasonId, matchweek.
   - Output: JSON with pagination and data[] of matches (kickoff time, teams, ground, matchId, etc.).
   - Typical flow: Use after pl_standings or pl_teams_in_competition to build a matchweek view; pass matchId values to pl_match_details for deep dives.

3) pl_teams_in_competition — club list/metadata
   - When: You need the list of clubs in a competition/season, with stadium and basic identity fields.
   - Input: competitionId, seasonId.
   - Output: JSON with pagination and data[] team objects (id, name, shortName, abbr, stadium, etc.).
   - Notes: Endpoint is paginated; routine returns the first page plus a _next token. If you need all clubs, use _next to page manually or post-process.
   - Typical flow: Call early to map Pulselive team IDs to human-readable club names and stadiums, then reuse those IDs in other routines.

4) pl_team_overview_bundle — club metadata (branding/context)
   - When: You need rich club-level metadata (founding year, stadium name, official site, social handles, shirt URLs) for a single team.
   - Input: teamId (Pulselive team identifier).
   - Output: JSON with a top-level metadata object containing club_established, club_stadium, club_website, club_instagram_handle, club_tiktok_handle, club_x_handle, shirt_url, shirt_url_pl, etc.
   - Typical flow: Use alongside pl_teams_in_competition (to discover teamId) and pl_standings (for sporting context) to build full team overview cards.

5) pl_player_profile_and_stats — player profile (no confirmed stats)
   - When: You need detailed player profile/historical info from the public /api/v1/players/{playerId} endpoint.
   - Input: playerId.
   - Output: An array of season-specific records with currentTeam, country, name, shirtNum, physical attributes, dates, and id fields.
   - Notes: Despite the name, only the profile endpoint is confirmed; season stats from the v2 stats endpoint could not be reliably validated in this environment. Treat this as a profile-only routine.
   - Typical flow: Use after you have playerIds from elsewhere (e.g., match lineups from pl_match_details) to enrich UIs with player bios.

6) pl_match_details — events and lineups
   - When: You need rich detail for a specific match, including event timeline and lineups.
   - Input: matchId.
   - Output: A bundled object { events, lineups } where each part is the parsed JSON from Pulselive events and lineups endpoints (home_team, away_team, players, cards, subs, goals, etc.).
   - Typical flow: Combine with pl_fixtures_by_matchweek (to discover matchIds) to power match-centre pages, live blogs, or analytics.

How to combine routines in practice:
- To build a league overview page: call pl_standings for the primary table, then pl_teams_in_competition to get club details, and optionally pl_team_overview_bundle per club for branding and external links.
- To build a matchweek schedule with deep links: use pl_fixtures_by_matchweek to list matches; for any match the user opens, call pl_match_details to show events and lineups; use pl_player_profile_and_stats on interesting players from those lineups.
- To build a club profile page: start from a known teamId (from pl_teams_in_competition); call pl_team_overview_bundle for metadata; optionally show recent fixtures via pl_fixtures_by_matchweek filtered client-side by that team, and standings context from pl_standings.

General guidance:
- All routines target public, unauthenticated GET APIs observed on premierleague.com; they are suitable for read-only scraping and data integration.
- Parameters are designed to mirror Pulselive IDs (competitionId, seasonId, teamId, playerId, matchId). Where you don’t know an ID, use another routine (e.g., teams or fixtures) to discover it first.
- Responses are raw JSON from the upstream APIs with minimal transformation; downstream code should handle pagination, error envelopes, and any additional filtering or joining as needed.

arguments.usage_guide:
This catalog exposes a set of high-value, read-only scraping routines around the public Premier League (Pulselive + api.premierleague.com) APIs observed on premierleague.com. They are designed to be composed together.

1) pl_standings — league tables
- Purpose: Get the official standings table for a competition/season.
- Inputs: competitionId (e.g., 8 for Premier League), seasonId (e.g., 2025).
- Output: JSON with matchweek and tables[].entries including team object and overall/home/away stats (played, won, drawn, lost, goals, points, positions).
- Use when: You need league tables, form guides, or to derive team ranks/points for analytics.

2) pl_fixtures_by_matchweek — fixtures/schedule by round
- Purpose: List all matches in a given matchweek for a competition/season.
- Inputs: competitionId, seasonId, matchweek.
- Output: JSON with pagination and data[] matches (kickoff time, teams, ground, matchId, etc.).
- Use when: Building matchweek views, schedule pages, or selecting a matchId for deeper inspection.
- Combine with: pl_match_details (for a chosen matchId), pl_team_overview_bundle (for team branding), pl_player_profile_and_stats (for key players).

3) pl_teams_in_competition — club directory
- Purpose: Get the list of teams in a competition/season with core metadata.
- Inputs: competitionId, seasonId.
- Output: JSON with pagination and data[] team objects (id, name, shortName, abbr, stadium details).
- Notes: Paginated; routine returns first page and a _next token. For all teams, page manually using that token.
- Use when: You need to map Pulselive team IDs to human-readable clubs, build club pickers, or join with standings/fixtures.

4) pl_team_overview_bundle — club metadata/branding
- Purpose: Retrieve rich club metadata from the Pulselive metadata endpoint.
- Inputs: teamId.
- Output: JSON with top-level metadata containing club_established, club_stadium, club_website, social handles, shirt URLs, etc.
- Use when: Building team overview cards or enriching tables/fixtures with official branding and external links.
- Combine with: pl_teams_in_competition (to discover teamId), pl_standings (for performance context).

5) pl_player_profile_and_stats — player profiles (profile-focused)
- Purpose: Fetch detailed player profile data from /api/v1/players/{playerId}.
- Inputs: playerId.
- Output: Array of season records with currentTeam, country, name, shirt number, physical attributes, dates, and id fields (competitionId, seasonId, playerId).
- Notes: Stats endpoint could not be reliably validated; treat this as a profile-only scraper despite the name.
- Use when: You have a playerId (e.g., from match lineups) and need biography/history info.

6) pl_match_details — events + lineups bundle
- Purpose: Get rich per-match detail: event timeline plus lineups.
- Inputs: matchId.
- Output: { events, lineups } combined from Pulselive events and lineups endpoints, each including home_team and away_team structures with players, goals, cards, substitutions, etc.
- Use when: Powering match-centre UIs, analytics, or highlight tools that need full context for a single match.
- Combine with: pl_fixtures_by_matchweek (to discover matchIds), pl_player_profile_and_stats (for players in the lineups).

7) pl_broadcast_schedule — TV/broadcast listings
- Purpose: Retrieve official broadcasting events for a date range.
- Inputs: from, to (YYYY-MM-DD), page, pageSize.
- Output: JSON with pageInfo and content[] broadcasting events (id, name, startDateTime, broadcasters, channels, contentReference linking to matches/content).
- Use when: Building TV listings, broadcast planners, or adding broadcast context to fixtures.

8) pl_content_search — content discovery
- Purpose: Search Premier League articles and videos with pagination and filters.
- Inputs: offset, pageSize, contentTypes (e.g., VIDEO,TEXT), sort, sortOrder.
- Output: JSON with pageInfo and content[] items (id, type, title, description, metadata, etc.).
- Use when: Building news feeds, search pages, or editorial dashboards.

9) pl_playlist_items — curated rails/playlists
- Purpose: Fetch the items in a specific Premier League content playlist.
- Inputs: playlistId, pageSize.
- Output: Playlist object with metadata and items[] (id, type, sid) plus pageInfo.
- Use when: Reproducing curated rails (e.g., Latest News, Featured Videos) or reusing editorial groupings in your own UI.

How to use these together
- League dashboard: pl_standings + pl_teams_in_competition + pl_team_overview_bundle.
- Matchweek hub: pl_fixtures_by_matchweek → for each match, pl_match_details; enrich players via pl_player_profile_and_stats.
- Club page: pl_team_overview_bundle for branding, pl_standings for table position, pl_fixtures_by_matchweek filtered client-side for that team, and relevant content via pl_content_search or pl_playlist_items.
- Media/broadcast view: pl_broadcast_schedule for TV slots, link events to matches via contentReference, and surface related articles/videos via pl_content_search or pl_playlist_items.

General notes
- All routines wrap public GET endpoints; no auth tokens are required.
- IDs (competitionId, seasonId, teamId, playerId, matchId, playlistId) come from these APIs themselves; use list-style routines (teams, fixtures, content search, playlists) to discover them.
- Responses are returned as close as possible to the upstream JSON; your application should handle pagination and any error envelopes as needed.
